working_title: County Down's Golf Coast: A Practical Guide to Playing Royal County Down, Ardglass, Kirkistown Castle and Warrenpoint
angle: Northern Ireland's County Down is home to what many rank as the world's finest links, but most visiting golfers fly in, play Royal County Down, and fly straight back out. This post makes the case for treating the county as a proper golf circuit, pairing the unmissable headliner with three very different and far more affordable courses across the Mourne coastline and Ards Peninsula.
research_notes:
- Royal County Down (Newcastle): founded 1889, designed by Old Tom Morris with later input from Harry Vardon and Harry Colt. Championship Links par 71, 7,186 yards, slope 142. Visitor green fee £450 in 2026 (confirmed via royalcountydown.org). Also has 18-hole Annesley Links (par 66, 4,617 yards), green fee £120 in 2026. Visitor play on Championship Course available Mon, Tue, Thu (mornings), Fri, Sun (afternoons) — not Wednesdays or Saturdays. All groups must have a minimum of one caddie. Full payment required at booking; non-refundable. Consistently ranked in world top 5.
- Ardglass Golf Club: 18-hole cliff-top links, par 70, 6,268 yards, founded 1896. Sits on Ardglass coastline about 30 minutes from Royal County Down, under an hour from Belfast. Clubhouse occupies a fortified building with origins dating to 1405 — reputedly among the oldest buildings used as a golf clubhouse in the world. Irish Sea comes into play on 8 holes and is visible from all 18. Visitors welcome. Considered a strong-value alternative to RCD — exact current green fee not confirmed in search results, do not state a specific figure.
- Kirkistown Castle Golf Club (Cloughey, Ards Peninsula): James Braid layout (1934), founded 1902. Par 69, 6,167 yards. The most easterly 18-hole course on the island of Ireland and the nearest links to Belfast (approx 45 minutes). Area has the lowest rainfall in Northern Ireland; free-draining sandy base means playable year-round. Signature hole: par-4 10th at 435 yards, reputed to be one of the hardest par 4s in Irish golf. Weekday green fees from around £35, weekend from around £40 (Golfshake data — treat as indicative, verify before publish). Recognised as Best Value Golf Experience in Ulster.
- Warrenpoint Golf Club: 18-hole parkland, par 71, 6,173 yards, founded 1893. Overlooks Carlingford Lough with Mourne Mountains backdrop. Best visitor days: Mon, Thu, Fri, Sundays. Handicap certificate required. Has hosted Irish Professional Championship and Ladies European Tour event. Weekday green fee around £38, weekend around £45 (thestimp.co.uk data — treat as indicative). Produced notable Irish professionals including Ronan Rafferty.
- Getting there: Belfast City Airport (BHD) approx 30–40 minutes from Newcastle/Downpatrick by car. Belfast International (BFS) approx 1 hour. Newcastle is approx 45 minutes south of Belfast via the A24. Ferry options from mainland GB: Stena Line and P&O serve the Belfast/Larne routes from Cairnryan (formerly Stranraer). A car makes the circuit far more practical — courses are spread across the county and not well linked by public transport.
- Accommodation: Slieve Donard Resort & Spa in Newcastle is the obvious base for RCD (adjacent to the first tee). Burrendale Hotel in Newcastle is a more mid-range option also used in golf packages.
- Context: The Open returned to Northern Ireland (Royal Portrush) in 2025, likely lifting the profile of the whole region for UK golf travellers.
